gate.description: Task 1's S1 (fluid_editor does not auto-commit), S3 (engine:commit_text accepts arbitrary text) and S11 (the Enter -> preview -> Enter loop closes) are life-or-death. S1 or S3 falsified means Plan A' does not exist: stop implementing and return to design to evaluate Plan B' (design §3.5). S11 falsified means design §6.1-§6.2 must go back to design review before any implementation continues; Plan A' itself may still stand. S11 was added to the gate by decision D3 (design §13, 2026-09-20).
gate.blocks: all implementation code for Tasks 2-12 (anything under rime/ or tests/)

tasks.name: Phase 0 spike
tasks.description: Verify the foundations Plan A' rests on. Throwaway probe code; nothing enters the repo.
acceptance: S9 io.popen can run curl from inside rime-lua
S10 multi-file require works
S3 engine:commit_text exists and commits arbitrary text (life-or-death)
S4 ctx:set_property/get_property round-trips
S1 fluid_editor does not commit segment selections to the app (life-or-death)
S2 whether Chinese punctuation merges into the composition (either answer lets work continue)
S5 key_binder select: switches schemas both ways
S6 ShadowCandidate comment change takes effect
S7 long preedit behaviour per app: Terminal, WeChat, Slack, Chrome
S11 the Enter -> preview -> Enter loop closes in both draft states (fully confirmed, last segment open) for at least one display mechanism, and the report names which (life-or-death)
S13 a blocking Enter measured at 1.5s and 4s in WeChat, Slack and Terminal: Enter must not reach the application at 1.5s, and keys typed during the stall arrive afterwards in order
S12 focus loss recorded per app: what lands in the input box and whether the draft survives (evidence for decision D2)
S14 mixed content typed into the draft recorded: an identifier with capitals, a URL, an emoji (evidence for R13)
S8 backend latency baseline translate vs apfel, cold and warm recorded separately
Report records actual Squirrel / librime / librime-lua / macOS versions
All probes removed; the IME is back to a clean state

tasks.name: Scaffolding + JSON string encoding
tasks.description: Directories, the test runner, json.escape and json.shq.
acceptance: lua tests/test_json_encode.lua prints 10 assertions OK
json.shq uses POSIX single quotes, not string.format('%q', ...)

tasks.name: JSON decoding
acceptance: lua tests/test_json_decode.lua passes every assertion
Malformed input returns nil plus an error message string; never raises
Both real OpenAI and Anthropic response shapes yield the translation

tasks.name: Phase constants and error strings
tasks.description: state.lua: three phase constants plus eight error-code strings. Holds no state object.
acceptance: lua tests/test_state.lua passes every assertion
state.new does not exist (negative assertion: no regression to a module-singleton FSM)
The eight error strings match design §8.1 word for word

tasks.name: Config loading and validation
tasks.description: config.load: flat YAML subset parsing, defaults, tiered-trust validation.
acceptance: lua tests/test_config.lua passes every assertion
timeout_ms defaults to 1500 (not 3000)
max_chars counts characters, not bytes
allow_remote=false plus a non-loopback base_url is refused
allow_remote=true plus non-loopback http:// is refused; https:// is allowed
No toggle_keycode / toggle_modifier exist

tasks.name: Backend adapters
tasks.description: backend.translate plus three adapters (openai / libretranslate / anthropic), the curl runner, error classification, and the prewarm no-op.
acceptance: lua tests/test_backend.lua passes every assertion
Three adapters x eight error codes fully covered
temperature carried only by the openai adapter (design §7.7)
anthropic sends anthropic-version, a top-level system field, and a required max_tokens
anthropic reads the result by walking content[] for type=='text', never content[0]
The api key never appears in any log or error string
prewarm is an empty function

tasks.name: Session state and draft snapshot
tasks.description: session.lua: a wrapper over Context properties plus draft snapshot comparison.
acceptance: lua tests/test_session.lua passes every assertion
All state goes through Context properties; no session state left at module level
session.stale judges correctly for both draft-differs and snapshot-missing

tasks.name: Pure-function key decisions
tasks.description: decide.decide(key, phase, draft_empty) -> action. Touches no rime global, does no IO, mutates no state.
acceptance: lua tests/test_decide.lua passes every assertion
Covers Enter in all three phases, Shift+Enter, Esc, any other key, release events, and Enter with modifiers
Any other key is always invalidate_and_pass (catch-all, no key enumeration)
There is no toggle branch

tasks.name: Rime glue layer
tasks.description: shared / processor. The processor alone owns committing and writes the display into segment.prompt (decision D1).
acceptance: lua tests/test_glue_load.lua passes (both modules load with the right export shape)
engine:commit_text appears only in ime_translate_processor.lua
shared has no fsm / phase (negative assertion: session state stays out of module singletons)
Both invalidation checks present: decide, and the top of every processor event, which also clears the prompt (design §6.2, decision D1)
Every ctx:clear() is preceded by a commit_text (never eat text)

tasks.name: Schema wiring + installer + LaunchAgent + first real-machine smoke
tasks.description: The schema, default.custom.yaml, user config defaults, install.sh and the translate LaunchAgent, installed and working.
acceptance: Every real-machine smoke check in plan Task 10 Step 6 passes: gate rows as specified, record rows once the observation is written down
install.sh is idempotent: two runs give the same result and never overwrite user config
install.sh preserves the ime_translate/ subdirectory rather than flattening it
rime/ime_translate.yaml contains no secret, only api_key_account

tasks.name: README + compatibility matrix + translate evaluation
tasks.description: User documentation (features 001 and 002), the application x check matrix observed by the agent and confirmed by the user, and a 30-sentence evaluation of the default backend, translate.
acceptance: Every matrix cell is one of supported / needs config / unverified; none blank
The 30-sentence set covers chat, code identifiers, URLs, emoji and mixed Chinese-English
translate evaluated on the 30 sentences: each translation judged acceptable or not (the agent first, the user confirms), with P50/P95 recorded
The eval's conclusion on the default backend (D4: translate) is written into docs/compat-matrix.md and design §2

tasks.name: Wrap-up and documentation write-back
tasks.description: Full test run, clean-machine reinstall verification, and folding the spike verdicts and backend choice back into the design set.
acceptance: scripts/run_tests.sh all PASS, exit code 0
After a clean reinstall, the core checks K1-K12 pass (agent-run, confirmed by the user); install.sh is idempotent and leaves the user config unchanged
design §2 backend, §5.3 punctuation, §10.2 S1-S14, §12 risks, §15 F-rows and the status line are all written back
overview.md status changes from 'awaiting Phase 0 spike verification' to 'verified, v1 usable'
